events.title: Antony and Octavian fight Brutus and Cassius at Philippi
events.description: In the first battle of Philippi, Mark Antony defeated Cassius and took his camp, while Brutus overran Octavian's troops. The battle was a tactical draw, but Cassius, believing it lost, took his own life to avoid capture.

events.title: Theodosius I settles the Goths inside the Roman Empire
events.description: Emperor Theodosius I concluded a treaty allowing the Goths to settle south of the Danube as semi-autonomous allies. Giving a whole people land within the frontier set a precedent that reshaped the late Roman world.

events.title: Heraclius the Younger's rebel fleet reaches Constantinople
events.description: The fleet of Heraclius the Younger, who with his father, the Exarch of Africa, had rebelled against Emperor Phocas in 608, reached Constantinople. Heraclius went on to execute Phocas and be proclaimed emperor, founding the Heraclian dynasty.

events.title: Francis of Assisi dies at the Porziuncola
events.description: Francis of Assisi died at the Porziuncola chapel below Assisi. The merchant's son who embraced radical poverty had founded the Franciscan order, and he was canonised less than two years later.

events.title: Dafydd ap Gruffydd, last native Prince of Wales, is executed
events.description: Dafydd ap Gruffydd, who had claimed the title Prince of Wales after his brother Llywelyn's death, was hanged, drawn and quartered at Shrewsbury on the orders of Edward I. He was the last native Prince of Wales before Edward's conquest.

events.title: Muhammad VII becomes the twelfth Nasrid ruler of Granada
events.description: Muhammad VII, son of Yusuf II and grandson of Muhammad V, came to the throne of the Emirate of Granada on his father's death. In 1394 he defeated an invasion by the Order of Alcántara, then restored peace with Henry III of Castile.

events.title: Earl Van Dorn attacks Rosecrans at the Second Battle of Corinth
events.description: Confederate forces under Earl Van Dorn attacked the Union defences around Corinth, Mississippi, in a battle that lasted two days. For the second time in the Iuka–Corinth Campaign, William S. Rosecrans defeated a Confederate army.

events.title: Lincoln proclaims a national day of Thanksgiving
events.description: Amid the Civil War, Abraham Lincoln proclaimed the last Thursday of November a national day of thanksgiving. The proclamation answered years of campaigning by the editor Sarah Josepha Hale and began an annual federal holiday.

events.title: King Alexander renames his realm the Kingdom of Yugoslavia
events.description: Alexander I renamed the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes as Yugoslavia, 'land of the South Slavs', as part of his royal dictatorship. The new name was meant to override the national rivalries dividing the state.

events.title: Germany is reunified
events.description: The German Democratic Republic acceded to the Federal Republic, reuniting Germany 45 years after its division. The peaceful merger, less than a year after the Berlin Wall opened, marked the close of the Cold War in Europe.
